summary: Riika J. Virtanen is a Tibetologist who conducted her doctoral studies at the University of Helsinki under supervisors Asko Parpola, Klaus Karttunen, and Hannu Riikonen, and studied under teacher Sangye Tandar Naga.

Rikizan Ishikawa (1943–1997) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from around 1962 to 1971. He served as Professor of Buddhist Studies at Komazawa University from around 1980 to 1997.

Ringu Tulku is a Buddhist studies scholar and Tibetologist who studied at Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, the 16th Karmapa, and Tubten Tsondru. He founded Bodhicharya.

Rinzin Thargyal is a scholar in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He earned his Magister degree at the University of Oslo in 1985, studying under supervisors Fredrik Barth and Arne Martin Klausen.

Rita Langer is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. She studied at SOAS, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and the University of Hamburg (PhD 2004). She has held posts at the University of Bristol.

Rita M. Gross (1943–2015) was a religious and Buddhist studies scholar. She studied at UW–Milwaukee and the University of Chicago (PhD). She held positions at UW–Madison (~1977–1979) and UW–Eau Claire (~1979–1998) as Professor of Philosophy and Religious Studies.

Rizong Sras Rinpoche (1927–2022) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He completed monastic training at Drepung Loseling Monastery under the 14th Dalai Lama, Losal Ling Khen Zur Jampal Sampel, and Pema Gyaltsen, later serving as abbot there and at Gyume.

Rob Linrothe is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Minnesota and the University of Chicago (PhD ~1992). He held faculty posts at Skidmore College (1992–2009) and Northwestern University (2010–2022).

Rob Nairn (1939–2023) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Zimbabwe, University of London, and University of Edinburgh. He served as senior lecturer at the University of Zimbabwe and professor of law and criminology at the University of Cape Town.

Robert A. F. Thurman is a Buddhist studies scholar and Tibetologist. He studied under Geshe Wangyal, the 14th Dalai Lama, and others. He held posts at Amherst College (1973–1988) and Columbia University (1988–2019), and founded the American Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Robert Alan Goodding is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied under doctoral supervisor Patrick Olivelle at the University of Texas at Austin, earning his PhD in 2002.

Robert Alexander Neil (1852–1901) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Aberdeen and Peterhouse, Cambridge. He served as University Lecturer in Sanskrit at Cambridge from 1884 and as a Fellow of Pembroke College, Cambridge, in 1900.

Robert Anthony Orsi is a religious studies scholar and historian. He studied at Trinity College and Yale University. He held academic posts at Fordham (1981–1988), Indiana University (1988–2001), Harvard (2001–2007), and Northwestern University from ~2007.

Robert B. Ekvall (1898–1983) was a Tibetologist who held posts at the University of Chicago (~1953–1956), the University of Washington (1958), and the Burke Museum of Natural History and Culture (~1963–1978).

Robert Baker Aitken (1917–2010) was a scholar and teacher of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and UC Berkeley, and held posts at Besant Hill School, the University of Hawaiʻi, and the East-West Center.

Robert Barnett is a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Cambridge (~1973–1976). He held academic posts at Columbia University (~1999–2018), SOAS University of London (~2018), and King's College London (~2018).

Robert Caesar Childers (1838–1876) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Wadham College, Oxford, and under Yatramulle Dhammarama Thera. He served at the India Office and as Professor of Pali at University College London (~1872–1876).

Robert Chalmers (1858–1938) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Oriel College, Oxford, and under T. W. Rhys Davids. He served as president of the Royal Asiatic Society (1922–1925) and Master of Peterhouse, Cambridge (1924–1931).

Robert Chambers (1737–1803) was an Indology scholar who studied at Lincoln College, Oxford. He was Vinerian Professor of English Law at Oxford (1766), Principal of New Inn Hall (1766), Chief Justice in Bengal (~1789–1798), and president of The Asiatic Society (~1797–1799).

Robert Charles Zaehner (1913–1974) worked in religious studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. Educated at Christ Church, Oxford, and Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey, he was Oxford's Professor of Eastern Religions and Ethics and an All Souls fellow from 1952.
